Devi Ever FX browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal events 2014 Summer NAMM 2014 Devi Ever FX BDSM - Big Distortion Sound Machine Published on July 19, 2014 Devi Ever FX distortion pedal Summer NAMM 2014 Summer NAMM 2014 picture by Gearphoria Summer NAMM 2014 Information Devi Ever FX The Big Distortion Sound Machine! A first for DE:FX - parallel distortion. One input is sent to two fuzz circuits, The Ruiner and the Torn's Peaker. The output of these circuits are mixed down to OUT 2. Or, for the immersive experience, hook up OUT 1 and OUT 2 to their own amps, or even more pedals and then amps! STEREO DESTRUCTION. The Ruiner is one of our greatest hits, effectively converting any input into a brassy, bassy square wave. Throw a chord at it an listen to it glitch! You can also roll back the gain for less destruction, but really, how often is that called for? The Torn's Peaker is the "deluxe version" found in our TP/AE Hybrid. That means a WORSE toggle for super clipping sizzles. Zazz knob for textural changes. TP/AE knob for subtle gain and tone shifts. And plenty of volume. Designed for ultimate bass guitar domination, but also quite effective with guitars and other less woofy instruments. $200 MSRP Devi Ever FX (press release, October 24, 2014) We are super excited to release the first brand spanking new pedal from Devi Ever FX since we took over, the Big Distortion Sound Machine. This monster combines two popular circuits, the Ruiner and Torn's Peaker/Aenima into a fuzz to EAT THE MIX.  The circuits are parallel to one another, so you can send both to OUT 2 or you can send them each to their very own amplifier for STEREO DESTRUCTION. The Ruiner side of the pedal produces a super compressed deep bass blast not unlike a square wave.  The Torn's Peaker/Aenima provides a wide variety of scratchy treble blasting noise fuzzes, as well as subtler, more organic and traditional tones.  The "worse" toggle is handy for jumping between these general arenas of sound. Our Big Distortion Sound Machine was engineered to create a full frequency assault with a bass guitar, but it's just as pleasurable on guitar.
